en: The Eight Verses on the Holy Gaṅgā
Oṃ! O Blessed One, on your banks, subsisting on water alone and free from thirst for sense-objects, I worship Kṛṣṇa— O Gaṅgā,
who serves as the staircase to heaven and destroys all impurities!
O Goddess Gaṅgā, with your most tremulous waves, be gracious! ||1||

O Blessed One, crown of the play of worldly existence, those living beings who touch even a minute drop of your water become the bearers of the chowries for the celestial women of the city of the gods.
They roll upon the lap that is free from the stains and terrors of the Kali age. ||2||
Shattering the cosmic egg, causing the matted locks on Śiva’s head to flourish,
falling from the sky, tumbling from the sloping crags of the caves of the Golden Mountain,
rolling upon the surface of the earth, and utterly crushing the dense armies of the host of sins— [so may she protect you].
May the purifying river of the city of the gods, filling the ocean of the sky, sanctify us. ||3||

The water on its banks is darkened at dawn and dusk by swarms of bees intoxicated by the scent of rut-wine dripping from the temples of bathing elephants; it is tawny with the clinging saffron falling from the breasts of bathing celestial women, and its surface is strewn with heaps of kuśa grass and flowers gathered by sages.
The water of the Gaṅgā, with its waves agitated by the trunks of young elephants, was drunk. ||4||
First, it was the water in the vessel for the ritual rites of the Primordial Grandfather;
afterwards, it was the purifying water from the feet of the Lord reclining upon the serpent;
and further, it is this [Ganges], the jewel adorning the matted locks of Śambhu, belonging to the great seer Jahnu.
The divine Bhāgīrathī, the maiden who destroys all impurity, is seen. ||5||
Descending from the king of mountains, rescuing people sinking in her own waters, sporting across the near and far shores, dispelling the entire series of fears of worldly existence,
resembling the serpent Śeṣa, and appearing like a leaf upon the head of Hara— [salutations to her].
Victorious is the enchanting Gaṅgā, who dwells on the outskirts of Kāśī.

Whence is the wave for you, O Gaṅgā, if you have come within the range of my vision? You bestow the yellow-robed Lord whose abode is the peak of Meru; if the body of embodied beings falls into your lap, it attains liberation.
Then, O Mother, even the attainment of the station of Indra (Śatakratu) would be exceedingly trivial. ||7||

O Gaṅgā, essence of the three worlds, whose vast waters are washed by all the celestial damsels, whose nature is the fullness of Brahman, who removes the dust from the feet of Hari, and who is the path to heaven—
if even a single drop of your water were the means of atonement for sins such as the killing of a Brāhmaṇa, [then what need is there for other penances]?
O Goddess Gaṅgā, who removes the sins of the three worlds, who is capable of praising you? Be gracious! 8.

O Mother Gaṅgā, when my life departs at the time of the body's end, may the pair of Nārāyaṇa’s feet become the object of my joyful remembrance as I place my joined palms upon the crown of my head on Your shore, while You are embraced by Śambhu.
May there be eternal, unswerving devotion, whose essence is the non-duality of Hari and Hara. ||9||
The man who, being self-restrained, recites this meritorious *Gaṅgāṣṭaka* goes to the world of Viṣṇu, completely liberated from all sins. (10)
Thus ends the Gaṅgāṣṭaka Stotra, composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Paramahaṃsa Parivrājaka Ācārya, the worshipful Śrī Govinda Bhagavatpāda.
